history.summary:
Modern lawn tennis originated in Birmingham, England, in the early 1870s, developed by Major Harry Gem and Augurio Perera, before being standardized and commercialized by Major Walter Clopton Wingfield in 1873. The All England Croquet and Lawn Tennis Club hosted the inaugural Wimbledon Championships in 1877, establishing the foundational rules, scoring system, and court dimensions that continue to define the sport today.

Following the historic advent of the Open Era in 1968—which permitted professionals to compete alongside amateurs at the four Grand Slam tournaments—tennis experienced massive global commercialization. By 2026, the sport features fierce multi-surface rivalries led by a new generation of champions such as Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner, Alexander Zverev, Aryna Sabalenka, and Coco Gauff, alongside cutting-edge electronic line calling and global year-end championships.

key_eras.description: Founding of Wimbledon, the US National Championships, French Championships, and Australian Championships, dominated by pioneers like Bill Tilden, Suzanne Lenglen, and Don Budge.

key_eras.era: 1946–1979 (Post-War Champions & Dawn of the Open Era)
key_eras.description: Rod Laver's two Calendar-Year Grand Slams, Billie Jean King's Battle of the Sexes and founding of the WTA, and the 1968 transition to the Open Era.
Iconic clashes between Borg-McEnroe, Navratilova-Evert, Sampras-Agassi, and Steffi Graf's historic 1988 Golden Slam.

key_eras.era: 2006–Present (The Big Three Dynasty & New Gen 2026 Era)
key_eras.description: Two decades of dominance by Federer, Nadal, Djokovic, and Serena Williams, transitioning into the 2026 era led by Alcaraz, Sinner, Zverev, Sabalenka, and Gauff.

major_tournaments.name: Wimbledon Championships
major_tournaments.description: The oldest and most prestigious tennis tournament in the world, celebrated for its grass courts, strict all-white dress code, and royal heritage.

major_tournaments.name: US Open
major_tournaments.description: The final Grand Slam of the calendar year held in New York, renowned for electric night sessions at Arthur Ashe Stadium.

major_tournaments.name: Roland Garros (French Open)
major_tournaments.description: The premier clay-court championship in Paris, testing physical endurance, sliding movement, and tactical patience.

major_tournaments.name: Australian Open
major_tournaments.description: The 'Happy Slam' opening each season in Melbourne, where Carlos Alcaraz completed the Career Grand Slam in January 2026.
